_comment: Standing record of adversarial lead audits. gate.sh reads this so a green gate cannot coexist with an unsendable lead list. Update it only by running the audit again, never by hand.

audits.note: First audit. Six failure modes named: URL-prefix instead of operation; vendor-owned or generated SDK code; anchor on a declaration rather than a call; changed field absent from the repo; vendored dependency trees; line numbers from a different revision. All six gated.

Re-audit after gating all six. Same rate. The gates changed WHY leads die, not HOW OFTEN. Root cause named: verification proved co-location and never dependence. Ten of twenty leads were one cluster where the call sites matched correctly and the change still could not affect them, because removing a 204 while the 200 remains narrows the API rather than breaking it. Fixed at the findings level.

Third audit, after the verifier was rebuilt around a dependence proof (call reaching the operation by method and full path template; or a read of the changed field traced back to a vendor call). The proof chains were judged accurate in every case -- the paths, methods and operations were right. The leads are still wrong, for a reason the rebuild did not address: operation reachability was accepted as sufficient for a whole-schema removal, so a caller who reaches the operation but never reads the removed schema's fields is reported as affected. Seven of ten fell that way. This audit also found a FINDINGS defect no previous round had named, described below.

findings_defect_found_and_fixed.what: OpenAPI security is a list of ALTERNATIVES: [{A}, {B}] means A or B. Both the engine and the independent precision checker flattened it to a set of scheme names, so adding an alternative scored as breaking.
findings_defect_found_and_fixed.evidence: Twilio DELETE /v2/Services/{Sid} went from [{accountSid_authToken}] to [{accountSid_authToken}, {access_token_bearer}]. Every existing caller kept working. Nine operations were scored breaking.
findings_defect_found_and_fixed.why_it_survived: The checker shared the engine's mistake, so it agreed with it. That is precisely the failure a separate checker exists to prevent, and it means the earlier 86/86 claim was wrong for the security class.
findings_defect_found_and_fixed.status: Fixed in both, independently. A change is breaking only when some old alternative can no longer be satisfied. Re-measured: 84 breaking findings, 84/84 confirmed, zero undecidable.

standing.blocker: Operation reachability is accepted as proof for a whole-schema removal. A caller who reaches the operation but never reads any field of the removed schema is not affected, and seven of ten audited leads were exactly that. The fix is to resolve the removed schema to its leaf field names in the OLD spec and require a read of one of them, rejecting calls whose response is discarded.
standing.findings_precision: 5-vendor gate population: 49/49 breaking, zero undecidable. ALL 21 registered vendors, measured for the first time 2026-08-20: 1487/1537 = 96.7% on independently decidable findings, 337 undecidable, over 1874 breaking findings. Started the day claiming 96.3% over 2766 findings, which was really 67.8%. The earlier 64/64 was a statement about five vendors, not about the engine.
also_open: operation_reached() stops at the first affected operation with a hit, in list order, so an alphabetically earlier DELETE whose response is discarded wins over a GET whose response is deserialized. Rank by whether the response is consumed.

A lead's breaks_on names the finding's representative operation while its proof names the operation the file actually calls, with nothing stating the two are related. This misled three auditors who had the repo, the spec and the source in front of them.
standing.note: The findings engine is verified. The lead pipeline is not. Do not send outreach built on leads until an audit clears.
standing.blocker_fix_implemented: The prescribed schema_removed fix is in dependence.py: a proof requires a read of one of the deleted schema's own field names, and generic names cannot carry it. NOT YET AUDITED — lead_precision and sendable stay as they are until a fourth adversarial audit runs. Note the product direction has moved to `apidrift scan` against a consented checkout, where the cold-lead vantage problem does not arise.

findings_defect_found_and_fixed_2.what: A schema is an implementation detail of an operation; a caller only ever sees the operation. Diffing schemas in isolation cannot tell a field being DELETED from a field being MOVED between two schemas that compose into the same operation, and the second breaks nobody.
findings_defect_found_and_fixed_2.evidence: OpenAI removed `ResponseProperties.reasoning` in this window while `POST /responses` accepted `reasoning` throughout — it moved to another arm of the same allOf. Found by running the new `apidrift scan` against Azure-Samples/python-openai-demos, which reported reasoning.py:38 as broken. Five of 84 breaking findings were this class (OpenAI 3, Stripe 2).
findings_defect_found_and_fixed_2.why_it_survived: measure_precision.py asked the schema-level question — 'is the field still in this schema?' — which is the same question the engine asked, so it agreed. Identical shape to the security OR-of-AND defect above.
findings_defect_found_and_fixed_2.status: Fixed in both, independently. The engine suppresses a removal when every affected operation still exposes the name; the checker now resolves each affected operation from the RAW document with its own resolver and refutes relocations on its own. Mutation-verified: with the engine's suppression disabled, the checker independently refutes exactly those 5 (23/28 = 82.1%).

findings_defect_found_and_fixed_3.what: A path parameter's NAME is OpenAPI-internal and never reaches the wire, exactly like a schema name. `/v2/Conversations/{Sid}` and `/v2/Conversations/{id}` produce byte-identical URLs for every concrete value, so renaming one moves no endpoint and breaks no caller. The same rename also surfaces as a param_removed plus a param_added_required, because a path parameter is positional in the URL rather than sent by name.
findings_defect_found_and_fixed_3.evidence: Twilio renamed {Sid}->{id} and {ConversationSid}->{ConversationId} across Conversations and ControlPlane. That produced 15 of 79 breaking findings, plus 4 more param-level findings once renamed operations began being diffed body-to-body. Zero of the 19 break anybody.
findings_defect_found_and_fixed_3.why_it_survived: dependence.paths_match() has ALWAYS normalised parameter names away when matching a caller's literal to a template — the engine knew names did not matter while PROVING and did not know it while DIFFING. measure_precision.py asked the spec author's question ('did the path string change?'), which is true for a rename. Third instance of a checker sharing the engine's assumption.
findings_defect_found_and_fixed_3.status: Fixed in engine and checker independently. Also fixed a false NEGATIVE found alongside it: a renamed operation was never diffed body-to-body, so a vendor renaming a parameter and tightening the operation in one release had the second change go entirely unreported.

scan_standing._comment: The scan is a different vantage point from the leads and needs its own record. An Impact is a claim about a REPO; a finding is a claim about a SPEC diff. They are measured separately.
scan_standing.corpus: 22 public repositories that genuinely call these five vendors, full checkouts
scan_standing.note: All four initial impacts were refuted by hand against the source and the raw spec, and all four classes are now gated: a read proving a request-side change (phasehq/console), a keyword argument on the repo's OWN constructor counted as a request body (phasehq/console), and two of the same in autoevals/agentops. Zero impacts across 22 repos is a MEASUREMENT, not an absence — the Plaid fixture control still fires at the right line with exit 1.
known_blind_spots: Dependence is provable in Python only. Callers in other languages are now COUNTED and reported as UNMEASURED rather than silently passing as clean — a TypeScript-only repo calling a deleted Plaid endpoint previously reported 'clean, exit 0'.
API version pinning is not modelled at all. A caller pinned to an older Stripe/Plaid version is not affected by a change to the latest, and nothing in the engine looks for a pin.
The relocation suppressor consults a field map flattened at MAX_DEPTH=2, so it cannot see a name nested deeper and abstains silently rather than marking the finding unchecked.
The spec cache is not fetched by default, so a scan can be run against a stale clone.
_Assignments is one flat module-level dict, so def-use tracing is scope-blind and flow-insensitive across function boundaries.
scan_standing.pr_blocker: No write path exists and none should be added before a fourth adversarial audit samples IMPACTS from scan.py against real repos. Opening a pull request into someone else's repository is a larger outward-facing act than sending an email, and gate.sh already refuses to let the email ship.

vendor_coverage.note: tools/vendor_check.py could not import until this session -- it was moved into tools/ and its sys.path and cache paths still pointed at the repo root, so every run died on line 12. The '20/22 working' number came from a copy that no longer exists.
vendor_coverage.unmeasured_reason: zero breaking findings in the window, so there is nothing to audit. Not a pass -- the report prints them as UNMEASURED rather than clean.
vendor_coverage.window_caveats: 14 of 21 carry one: an observed range shorter OR LONGER than requested (the old side is the last commit BEFORE the window, which for a quiet repo can be a year earlier -- openai 429d of 180d), or specs with no history behind them. sendgrid's HEAD is 2026-03-24, so its window ends five months before `asof`.

per_vendor_precision._note: zero breaking findings in the window, so nothing to audit. Printed as UNMEASURED, which is not a pass.

open_false_positive_classes._note: 50 findings the independent checker still refutes, by kind. Each is a real defect and none is fixed. Three adversarial audits diagnosed the first three correctly and every one of their proposed fixes was measured as UNSAFE -- one would have dropped all-vendor precision to 77.3% and refuted `stripe token.card.iin`.
known_mechanisms: flattener key identity: `oneOf[null, X]` collapsing to `$ref X`, a root `$ref X` becoming `allOf[X, ...]`, and union arms renamed by content -- a key vanishes while the payload is unchanged.

engine and checker both ask whether the string appears in a `required:[...]` array at the one node their path reaches, rather than whether a body that validated under OLD is rejected under NEW. An independent adjudication of that class put it at 43 TRUE / 124 FALSE, and found HALF the checker's own confirmations were also false positives.
endpoint_removed: the engine keys on METHOD+path and the checker on path alone. Their refuted sets are disjoint, so the 5 each is not the same 5.

findings_defect_found_and_fixed_5.what: A schema NAME never reaches the wire. `schema_removed` was 1007 of the 2766 breaking findings across all 21 vendors -- 36% of the population -- and the precision checker confirmed 1007 of 1007.
findings_defect_found_and_fixed_5.evidence: The checker's test was `name in schemas_of(old) and name not in schemas_of(new)`, the same question the engine asks and the SPEC AUTHOR's question. Asked the caller's way -- find every $ref to it in the OLD document and look at the same place in the NEW one -- 694 of the 1007 are refuted. Klaviyo inlined 208 single-value enums at the identical property; Cloudflare renamed 191 response envelopes in bulk; PayPal's error_409 lived only inside error_default, one restructure reported 92 times; Sentry's whole components table is vestigial because it publishes a DEREFERENCED spec.
findings_defect_found_and_fixed_5.why_it_survived: Fifth instance of the checker sharing the engine's question, and the largest by an order of magnitude. All-vendor precision was never 96.3%; it was 67.8%.
findings_defect_found_and_fixed_5.status: Fixed in engine and checker independently, four suppression classes (unreachable / relocated / renamed / subsumed), each decided by a different question. Every one has a mutation in BOTH directions.

findings_defect_found_and_fixed_6.what: A refuter whose precondition holds for 100% of inputs is a broken instrument, not a result.
findings_defect_found_and_fixed_6.evidence: The first version of the `unreachable` rule refuted any schema with no $ref pointing at it. Sentry's openapi-derefed.json contains ZERO occurrences of `"$ref"` in 3.2 MB, so the test was vacuously true for all 157 of its schemas. An adversarial audit showed it would have deleted a real break: DetailedOrganizationSerializerWithProjectsAndTeams is verbatim the 200 body of a PUT that still exists and lost seven required response properties.
findings_defect_found_and_fixed_6.why_it_survived: It did not -- it was killed before shipping, by an audit run specifically to attack the new rules. Recorded because the shape recurs: this is the same failure as 'zero results is a failed measurement until a control says otherwise', applied to a suppressor instead of a search.
findings_defect_found_and_fixed_6.status: Both engine and checker now count the document's linking constructs first and ABSTAIN when there are none, in their own separate states (`unreachable_unmeasurable` / UNDECIDABLE). Measured: Sentry is the only fully-dereferenced vendor in the corpus; every other carries 502-17,807 refs.
